title: Best Game Console (2026)
summary: The guide lists the top handheld game consoles for 2026, highlighting the Nintendo Switch 2 as the overall leader.
method: Products were selected from TechRadar, Tom’s Hardware, IGN, and PC Gamer reviews, prioritising items mentioned by multiple sites.
assumptions: Prices are omitted because none of the sources provide them.

products.name: Nintendo Switch 2
why: Nintendo’s latest portable hybrid is highlighted as the primary recommendation in TechRadar’s handheld guide.
It is also mentioned in Tom’s Hardware as a top handheld option with a free game deal.
products.desc: The Switch 2 is a hybrid console that can be used as a handheld or docked to a TV. It features a new controller layout and a larger screen than its predecessor. It does not include a built‑in dock for TV play.
products.benefit: Picture a family gathering where everyone can play together on a single screen. The Switch 2 offers a hybrid design that lets you play on a TV or on the go, making it ideal for shared moments. It also has a large library of games and a proven controller layout. The catch: it still relies on a proprietary dock for full TV play.
cons: Requires proprietary dock for TV play
products.skip_if: You need a fully portable device with long battery life

products.name: Asus ROG Xbox Ally X
why: IGN lists it as one of the best handheld gaming PCs.
PC Gamer notes its OLED screen as a standout feature.
products.desc: The Ally X is a handheld gaming PC that runs Windows and features an OLED display. It includes a new Xbox Full Screen Experience and a comfortable design. It does not have a built‑in dock for TV play.
products.benefit: Picture a solo gamer who wants a portable PC with a vibrant screen. The Ally X delivers a sharp OLED display and a comfortable grip, making long sessions more enjoyable. It also runs Windows, giving access to a wide range of PC games. The catch: it lacks a built‑in dock for TV play.
products.skip_if: You need a dock for TV play

products.name: MSI Claw 8 EX AI+
why: IGN lists it as one of the best handheld gaming PCs.
PC Gamer notes its high performance.
products.desc: The Claw 8 EX AI+ is a handheld gaming PC that runs Windows and features a powerful processor and AI enhancements. It offers high performance for AAA games. It does not have a built‑in dock for TV play.
products.benefit: Picture a hardcore gamer who wants to play the latest AAA titles on a portable device. The Claw 8 EX AI+ delivers high performance and AI features, making it suitable for demanding games. It also runs Windows, giving access to a wide range of titles. The catch: it lacks a built‑in dock for TV play.
products.skip_if: You need a dock for TV play

products.name: Xbox Series X
why: T3 calls the Series X “the most powerful console” and notes its strong backwards compatibility. It also mentions easy expandable storage.
The console’s design is described as uninspired, but performance outweighs aesthetics.
products.desc: The Series X is Microsoft’s next‑gen flagship. It has a 1 TB drive with about 800 GB usable, supports 4K gaming, and lets you add storage easily.
products.benefit: Picture a gamer who wants to play the latest titles at the highest settings without a PC. The Series X delivers the top performance in this guide and the most usable storage expansion options. It beats the One X and 360 Slim in raw power and the Elite controller in overall system capability. The catch: only about 800 GB of its 1 TB drive is usable.

products.name: Xbox One X
why: PCWorld describes the One X as “as powerful as many gaming PCs” and notes its small, quiet design.
It is priced at $500 in the review, making it cheaper than a comparable PC build.
products.desc: The Xbox One X is a compact console that offers 4K gaming. It includes a 1 TB hard drive and is quieter than larger models.
products.benefit: Picture a player who wants 4K games without spending on a full PC. The One X gives near‑PC power in a small box and costs less than a comparable desktop. It is the only console here with a 1 TB drive and a quiet profile, beating the Series X on price and the 360 Slim on performance. The catch: its hard drive isn’t ideal for modern games and the UI is still messy.
cons: Hard drive not ideal for modern games
products.skip_if: You need the absolute top performance

products.name: Xbox 360 Slim
why: TechRadar’s review highlights the console’s reduced size and mentions its noise and storage features.
It remains a viable older‑generation option.
products.desc: The Xbox 360 Slim is a smaller version of the original 360. It measures 270 mm and includes updated noise and storage handling.
products.benefit: Picture a family that already owns Xbox games and wants a smaller console for the living room. The 360 Slim’s reduced size and quieter operation make it easier to fit in tight spaces. It is the only older‑gen console in this list, offering a different price point than newer models. The catch: it lacks the power and 4K support of newer consoles.

verdict.line: Picture a family gathering where everyone can play together on a single screen. The Switch 2 offers a hybrid design that lets you play on a TV or on the go, making it ideal for shared moments. It also has a large library of games and a proven controller layout. The catch: it still relies on a proprietary dock for full TV play.
